objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Nucleus in reducing thermal stress and slowing down aging of the primary LED.
dependent_variables: LED luminosity at 25°C and 1000 hours of operation
controls: LED luminosity at 25°C and 0 hours of operation
LED luminosity at 25°C and 1000 hours of operation with a standard LED without Nucleus
baseline: LED luminosity at 25°C and 0 hours of operation
procedure: Prepare 10 sets of primary LEDs with Nucleus and 10 sets without Nucleus.
Place the LEDs in a controlled environment with a temperature range of 20-30°C, power supply of 1.5A, and ambient humidity of 50-60%.
Measure the initial luminosity of each LED at 25°C and 0 hours of operation.
Operate the LEDs for 1000 hours and measure the luminosity at 25°C.
Repeat the experiment for 5 times to ensure reliable results.
expected_result: A decrease in LED luminosity at 25°C and 1000 hours of operation by 5.2% ± 1.6% compared to the baseline value.
falsification_condition: LED luminosity at 25°C and 1000 hours of operation is greater than 95.8% of the baseline value.
sample_requirements: 10 sets of primary LEDs with Nucleus and 10 sets without Nucleus.
safety_constraints: Ensure proper handling and storage of the LEDs to prevent damage and electrical shock.
information_gain: The effectiveness of the Nucleus in reducing thermal stress and slowing down aging of the primary LED, and the potential for future improvements in LED design and thermal management.
